offer.say: Twenty-two years I've hit that machine where the dent is. Twenty-two years it's worked. This week I hit it and it looked at me. Machines shouldn't look at you, {owner}. The whole town's drinking hot chocolate. They're getting sticky. They're getting sweet. It's unnatural.

options.text: Why not just buy a new machine?
Have you tried hitting it somewhere else?

new.say: The Double-Double people want to put their machine in with their sign. And their cups. And their opinions. This one's ours. It just needs a hose and a prayer.

options.text: Ours it is. I'll fix it.

cheek.say: There's only one dent. That's the dent. A second dent would be chaos. Gus tried a second dent in 2016. Look what happened. Guestbook entry. Twice.

options.text: Fine, one dent. I'll find a fix.

decline.say: Tea is for the Legion. This is a hockey rink.

accepted.say: Try the dent first. Just to be sure. Then call Terry. He's my nephew. He's a plumber. His pager goes off a lot.

p_terry.say: He'll be at the Plungers game Thursday. Catch him before the pager. After the pager he's gone till Friday.

p_clean.say: A working machine on a sticky counter. That's like a new jersey on Big Gord. Clean it up.

complete.say: First cup's yours. Look at that. Brown. Hot. Bitter. Perfect. I flipped the sign myself. Three people clapped. One of them was Earl. He'll deny it.

options.text: Can I hit it where the dent is? Just once?

c_best.say: It isn't. It's the most loved, though. That's better.

c_earl.say: Twice. Small claps. Like a man applauding a funeral he approves of.

c_dent.say: Go on. Gently. There. Now you're staff.

done.say: Coffee's on. Coffee's always on now.
